title: Sounds
summary: An overview of new music releases from Arid, Moby, R.E.M., Van Morrison, Nina Hagen, and Rick Wade.

blocks.markdown:
## Sounds

Arid's new album

**All Things Come In Waves**

The album will be released at the beginning of April.

Arid's sound is comparable to that of Absynthe Minded, Ozark Henry, Admiral Freebee, or Zornik.

The outstanding voice of lead singer Jasper Steverlinck is often compared to Jeff Buckley or Freddie Mercury.

On March 28, the musical vegan from New York, Moby, will release his new album. It bears the promising title **Last Night**.

He will present 15 brand new pieces to the world and once again impressively confirm his reputation as an exceptional artist, that much can be revealed. In the next issue of *proud*, you can then win the album.

R.E.M. is releasing their first studio album in four years, titled **Accelerate**.

The album is a return to the guitar-driven modern rock beloved by fans.

Also, the new album by Van Morrison,

**Keep It Simple**, will be released on April 1.

Grown up in Belfast, many of the local music styles can be recognized in his new album.

The influences range from jazz, folk, blues, Celtic, country, and soul to gospel.

In 1977, Nina Hagen first came out in the FRG (West Germany) with this album, directly after leaving the GDR (East Germany). And it was like a revelation. No woman had rocked so rhyming and cheeky far and wide. Even the experts were heavily impressed, and for the next 2 years, Ms. Hagen seemed to have snatched the No. 1 spot in the German charts for herself.

## Sounds

If you're thinking of buying a car or going on a European tour with a friend this summer, you should definitely check out the recently released album **The Good, the Bad and the Deep** by Detroit's Rick Wade. Rick produces tracks that are consistently so relaxed and satisfying that even a dovecote seems like a luxury penthouse to us, as long as we combine this music with a good view. In this beautiful bar, made for infinite space, frequencies effortlessly float from the speakers, which we have often experienced. Avoid letting the transition fall short, rather than saving the idyll of this absolute feeling of freedom early. This is The E-House that even Mom would find good. Everything feels good just the way it is.
